the mechanisms of cellular stress responses and the regulation of cell death.

the role of stress granules in the regulation of cell survival and death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO-induced SGs have a dual role: they are initially cytoprotective but later become cytotoxic, depending on the balance between the cellular energy status and mTOR signaling.
the NO-induced SGs are type II SGs that are pro-death.
NO-induced SGs are a marker of cellular energy balance, which is critical for determining the fate of the cells, and that the composition of the SGs depends on the energy status of the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitric oxide-induced type II stress granules are linked to the disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis and energy balance.
the composition of NO-stress induced SGs is linked to the energy status of the cell and the balance of pro-death and pro-survival signals.
the composition and function (type I versus II) of SGs is determined by the nature of stress, the energy balance of the cell, and the ability of the cell to recover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of SGs is not static and that their assembly can be linked to cellular stressors that alter energy balance.
the composition of SGs can be manipulated in ways that can either protect or kill cells.
the assembly of stress granules is a highly regulated process, which is influenced by a variety of cellular stressors.
